issue.title: fix: Error propagation and errback calling for group-like signatures
issue.body:
## Description

Fix propagation of errors and errback calling from chord and group children. This changeset
supersedes #6226 and rolls in some of the test cases presented by @maxfenv in comments
on that PR.

Fixes #6220 and a few other issues discovered along the way.

I know how hard it is to find time to contribute to open source, and I just can't express how grateful I am for everyone who picked up this problem and put in the work I couldn't. Thank you 1000 times - you're all the best!!!
This is still occurring - experiencing this issue right now on Python 3.11.2 with Celery 5.3

@auvipy Good to see you guys are still keeping up with these old threads 😅

I think my local issue is related - but potentially not the same exact problem.

We have quite a complex workflow that nests tasks a few levels deep. We've discovered that the `on_error` handler for a chord is not called if within that chord, another chord is created, and a task within the inner chords header fails.

We are running a normal celery app with a redis backend through Docker. Python 3.11.2 and Celery 5.3

Note that the following examples are pulled from sample code within our application. If needed I can put a more well though example together - but the use case is so straightforward I don't feel it is necessary.

Given these tasks:

```
@celery_app.task
def generic_good_task(*args, **kwargs):
    logger.info('Generic good task called')


@celery_app.task
def generic_error_task(*args, **kwargs):
    logger.info('Error task called')
    raise Exception('Error task called')


@celery_app.task
def generic_long_task(*args, **kwargs):
    logger.info('Long task called')
    time.sleep(5)
    logger.info('Long task finished')
```

I've created this simplified example workflow:

```
def sample_main_workflow(*args, **kwargs) -> Signature:
    from mods.workflows import tasks

    return (
        tasks.generic_good_task.si()
        | chord(
            [
                tasks.generic_good_task.si()
                | chord(
                    [
                        tasks.generic_good_task.si()
                        | tasks.generic_error_task.si()
                    ],
                    tasks.generic_good_task.si()
                )
            ],
            tasks.generic_good_task.si()
        )
        | tasks.generic_good_task.si()
    )
```

So we have a chord which we will call outer_chord that has a header which contains another chord that we'll call inner_chord.

The inner_chord is setup to throw an exception. 

At the top most level, we have this workflow wrapper we use to execute all of our celery workflows:

```
return (
    workflow_factory(*args, **kwargs).on_error(workflow_error_handler.s(workflow.id))
    | workflow_success_handler.si(workflow.id)
).delay()
```

`workflow_factory` can be any number of similarly defined functions as I showed with `sample_main_workflow` - it is simple a function that returns a chain/group/chord, whatever a given workflow wants to execute - in this case it is our sample problematic workflow.

Basically, the `workflow_success_handler` will just print a line indicating the success handler was called, similarly the `workflow_error_handler` will print a line indicating it was called.

When I execute this workflow I expect the `workflow_error_handler` to be called, however instead I get two instances of the raised exception printed out to the celery logs. 

The first is the exception itself which I expect - the second is a ChordError. What I believe is happening is the inner_chord I defined earlier is capturing the error but has no error handler of its own to work with. And for some reason, when it throws it's error - the error handler I do have defined at the top level is not catching it as an error. Everything works as expected if we remove the outer_chord and only execute the inner_chord.

Let me know if this is similar enough to this issue to consider re-opening. A senior dev and myself have been chasing this issue around our code base for a week now so if there's a known fix - we are very open to hearing it.

It is worth noting we originally had our chords defined as chains and groups - however, this caused another/different issue where after each item of the group in question finished executing, it would kick off a new instance of the task that came after the group. We had 5 workflows in the group so we ended up with 5 instances of the workflow being executed. I tried to create a simple use case of this as well but have not been able to properly reproduce it outside of our app. All I can say for certain is that approach is not viable in our context.

There's a bunch more exception/traceback stuff showing in the logs - but the important piece is we see the line: 
`[2023-06-18 20:19:02,403: WARNING/ForkPoolWorker-7] -----------------------------------------------------------------------------------> Error handler called`

Proving our error handler has been called as expected. This is the behavior I expect my original example to follow.

## Minimally Reproducible Test Case

There are two files below `canvastest.py` and `main.py`, I run the example by first starting a local redis instance by running `docker run -p 6379:6379 redis` then I run the worker `celery -A canvastest worker` and the main application `python main.py` ```python from celery import Celery app = Celery('canvastest', backend='redis://localhost', broker='redis://localhost') @app.task(throws=(Exception,),) def t1(x): print("t1") return x @app.task(throws=(Exception,),) def t2(x): print("t2") raise Exception() return x @app.task(throws=(Exception,),) def t3(x): print("t3") return x @app.task() def error_handler(*args, **kwargs): print("Error handler") ``` ```python from canvastest import t1, t2, t3, error_handler from celery import chord if __name__ == '__main__': combined_task = chord((t1.s(1), t2.s(2)),t3.s()).on_error(error_handler.si()) combined_task() ```

# Expected Behavior The example consist of a chord with two tasks in the header, one in the callback, and with an attached error_handler. `chord((t1.s(1), t2.s(2)),t3.s()).on_error(error_handler.si())` When one of the tasks fail I expect that to trigger the error handler, and no further errors should be generated after that. (It's expected behavior that the tasks might fail due to external reasons occasionally, which is handled by the error_handler). I expect this behavior regardless of which of the three tasks fail. # Actual Behavior - If the callback task in the chord fails the error handler is called, and no other exceptions show up in the log. :heavy_check_mark: - If one of the tasks in the header fails, a ChordError exception is raised and corresponding stack traces is present in the worker log. This is a problem because it's not an actual error in the context of the application, since it's expected to (occasionally) happen and any logging needed would be handled by the error handler method rather than dumping a stack trace into the logs. So having this extra noise in the logs is not desirable. ```log [2023-04-20 14:01:31,667: WARNING/ForkPoolWorker-16] t1 [2023-04-20 14:01:31,668: WARNING/ForkPoolWorker-1] t2 [2023-04-20 14:01:31,675: ERROR/ForkPoolWorker-1] Chord '3336718d-57e3-41e0-b62d-4fad8ae9cc62' raised: ChordError('Dependency ffdd942e-cfe9-498f-a4b1-9d3a80a9ee45 raised Exception()') Traceback (most recent call last): File "/home/jerkern/celery_mre/.venv/lib/python3.10/site-packages/celery/app/trace.py", line 451, in trace_task R = retval = fun(*args, **kwargs) File "/home/jerkern/celery_mre/.venv/lib/python3.10/site-packages/celery/app/trace.py", line 734, in __protected_call__ return self.run(*args, **kwargs) File "/home/jerkern/celery_mre/canvastest.py", line 15, in t2 raise Exception() Exception During handling of the above exception, another exception occurred: Traceback (most recent call last): File "/home/jerkern/celery_mre/.venv/lib/python3.10/site-packages/celery/backends/redis.py", line 520, in on_chord_part_return resl = [unpack(tup, decode) for tup in resl] File "/home/jerkern/celery_mre/.venv/lib/python3.10/site-packages/celery/backends/redis.py", line 520, in resl = [unpack(tup, decode) for tup in resl] File "/home/jerkern/celery_mre/.venv/lib/python3.10/site-packages/celery/backends/redis.py", line 426, in _unpack_chord_result raise ChordError(f'Dependency {tid} raised {retval!r}') celery.exceptions.ChordError: Dependency ffdd942e-cfe9-498f-a4b1-9d3a80a9ee45 raised Exception() [2023-04-20 14:01:31,676: WARNING/ForkPoolWorker-1] Error handler ```
